claims.text: The initial MgAlCuZnGd alloy has a density below 6 g/cm3.
The as-cast MgAlCuZnGd alloy is predominantly a metastable solid solution.
The as-cast alloy contains incipient Mg-rich regions.
Isothermal aging at 350–450 °C accelerates decomposition of the metastable solid solution.
Isothermal aging produces finely dispersed Mg-rich intermetallic phases.
Aging increases the number density of Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates relative to the unaged state.
Aging makes the Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates more uniformly distributed.
Mg-rich intermetallic clusters act as preferential sites for oxide-scale formation.
Mg-rich intermetallic phases preferentially oxidize during high-temperature exposure.
Preferential oxidation of the Mg-rich phases generates a MgAl oxide scale.
The MgAl oxide scale is adherent and protective.
Aged samples form a more adherent and protective oxide scale during oxidation at 600 °C than the as-cast baseline.
The aging-induced phase evolution modifies electrochemical corrosion behavior relative to the as-cast alloy.
Aged samples have lower corrosion current density in 3.5% NaCl than the unaged baseline.
Excessive aging can coarsen the phases beyond the regime in which the proposed mechanism applies.
Complete homogenization lies outside the phase-evolution regime addressed by the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The prediction specifically requires reduced corrosion current density, whereas the falsification rule treats any alteration in corrosion kinetics as potentially sufficient, including deterioration; the decisive corrosion direction is therefore inconsistent.

The predicted outcome frames falsification as absence of correlated improvements in both oxidation and corrosion, while the formal rule uses ambiguous 'or' and 'and/or' logic that can falsify the hypothesis when only one response is absent.
